claim: For the open hard-core chain H_L(V)=K_L+V W on L-1 sites, beta=tau L^2, chemical potential lambda/L^2, J>0, tau in a compact subset of (0,infinity), lambda bounded, and V in any compact K subset (-4J,infinity), a common parameter-independent exact isometric embedding sends the normalized grand-canonical Gibbs state to the Tonks-Girardeau/free-Dirichlet-fermion Gibbs state in full trace norm, uniformly in tau, lambda, V.
proof: RESULT.txt §§2-4. Exact configuration-graph identity; gap-coordinate polar embedding; discrete H1/diagonal-trace liminf and collision-free recovery; common-space norm-resolvent and heat convergence; c K_L coercivity and uniform Fock/heat tails.
supplied_inputs: Finite chain, fixed J, compact parameter intervals. No eigenbasis or interacting spectrum is supplied.
acquired_inputs: The continuum free-fermion sine spectrum is derived. For the moving-coupling extension only, invoke the internally banked all-sector estimate outputs/research/sol_attractive_critical/proof.txt (1.2)-(1.3), valid for all g>=g_*>0 without an upper bound.
costs: Qualitative asymptotic theorem only; no computable finite-L convergence modulus, finite-L sampler, or Gibbs-preparation circuit. Uniform q cutoff follows (4.3). Continuum mode cutoff K=O(sqrt(log(1/epsilon))) at fixed J,tau_-,B; O(K) Bernoulli mode draws. Physical H energy is on scale L^-2 when the scaled thermal energy is bounded; no energy-norm archive is claimed.
baseline: Girardeau's established impenetrable-boson/free-fermion spectral mapping and XXZ-to-Lieb-Liniger scaling. Those do not by themselves prove this open finite-chain full-Fock trace topology.
falsifier: An exact violation of the finite configuration form identity, failure of the fixed-sector discrete form convergence, or failure of the stated all-sector imported estimate in the moving-g_L extension.

claim: Under the FA2-SA1 compact-gap assumptions, D(rho_{L,V}||rho_{L,0}) tends to zero uniformly in tau, lambda, and V; Pinsker gives trace distance convergence of the interacting state to the finite-L free reference.
proof: RESULT.txt §5. Uniform free-energy convergence on a larger compact V interval; convexity and fixed-step secant bounds imply uniform derivative convergence; exact Gibbs relative-entropy identity (5.1).
supplied_inputs: Same as FA2-SA1; the target V set must remain a positive distance above -4J so it sits in the interior of an enlarged compact interval containing 0.
acquired_inputs: The partition-function convergence follows from FA2-SA1 and Z>=1.
costs: Asymptotic o(1), no explicit rate. Uniformity constant depends on the gap from -4J through the enlarged interval and coercivity/tail bound. No relative-entropy claim is made when V approaches -4J with L.
baseline: Finite-dimensional Gibbs relative-entropy identity and convexity of log trace exponential.
falsifier: A counterexample to the uniform partition convergence or convex secant derivative bound under the specified fixed-gap compact hypotheses.

claim: If g_L=L(4J+V_L) tends to infinity while V_L remains bounded, the embedded full-Fock Gibbs states converge in trace norm to the Tonks/free-fermion state. Relative-entropy convergence to V=0 is proved only when V stays in a compact set bounded away from -4J.
proof: RESULT.txt §3 gives fixed-q convergence from the diverging diagonal penalty; §4 uses the separately banked no-upper-bound all-sector estimate for g>=g_*>0.
supplied_inputs: Sequence V_L and public compact tau,lambda sets.
acquired_inputs: Uniform full-Fock q-tail estimate from outputs/research/sol_attractive_critical/proof.txt, equations (1.2)-(1.3).
costs: No explicit convergence rate in g_L or L. The uniform q-tail constants depend on a fixed lower bound g_*>0, not on an upper bound; KL near the threshold needs a further contact estimate.
baseline: Finite positive g gives the repulsive Lieb-Liniger continuum family in outputs/research/sol_attractive_critical/continuum_limit.txt.
falsifier: Failure of the imported Gaussian sector tail, or a fixed-sector limit different from the zero-diagonal Dirichlet form when g_L diverges.

claim: Uniform convergence D(rho_{L,V_L}||rho_{L,V=0})->0 over every bounded sequence V_L>-4J with g_L=L(4J+V_L)->infinity.
counterexample: At lambda=0 choose finite g_j->infinity with f_infinity(g_j)->f_TG, d_j=f_infinity(g_j)-f_infinity(g_j+1)>0. Fixed-g LL partition convergence, free partition convergence, and convexity give thresholds L_j so -f'_L(g_j)>=d_j/2 and both relevant partition functions are within 1/j of their limits for every L>=L_j. Increase L_j so L_j d_j>=j, 4J L_j>=2g_j, and g_j/L_j<=1/j. Set g_L=g_j on [L_j,L_{j+1}) and V_L=-4J+g_L/L. Then g_L->infinity and V_L->-4J, so FA2-SA3 gives trace-norm convergence to Tonks, but the exact Gibbs identity gives D>=Jj-3/j on block j; hence relative entropy diverges.
audit: Independently checked by /root/sol_kls_consequences on 2026-10-08. The strict decrease d_j>0 follows because the finite-g two-particle ground state has nonzero contact trace; all other sector eigenvalues are nondecreasing in g. This is an existential diagonal sequence, not an effective finite-bit schedule.
supplied_inputs: The internally proved fixed-g finite-chain-to-Lieb-Liniger partition convergence, free XX partition convergence, monotone g-to-infinity form limit, and trace theorem FA2-SA3.
costs: No effective thresholds/rate are supplied; existence is sufficient to disprove uniform KL convergence. The sequence has V_L->-4J but g_L->infinity, with no claim on the optimal growth threshold for KL divergence.
baseline: Trace distance convergence does hold along the counterexample sequence. The result demonstrates that trace norm does not control this relative entropy under the changing reference Gibbs energy observable.
falsifier: A flaw in strict finite-g contact monotonicity, the fixed-g partition convergence, or the exact Gibbs identity; the independent audit found none under those dependencies.

claim: For the open L-1-site hard-core chain with H_L=Hcrit+(g_L/L)W-(lambda/L^2)N, beta=tau L^2, fixed J,tau>0, |lambda|<=B, and g_L->g<0, the full-Fock partition function satisfies L^(-2) log Z_L -> tau|g|. For every fixed K, P(N<=K)->0, in fact at most exp(-tau|g|L^2+o(L^2)); each fixed-m canonical sector contribution is O_m(1).
proof: ../negative_scaled_coupling/RESULT.txt §§1-4. The exact open-endpoint graph form gives Hcrit>=0. A product state with a width floor(sqrt(L)) spin-coherent boundary ramp has exact expectations <Hcrit>=2Jw(1-cos(pi/w)), <N>=L-w-2, and <W>=L-(3/2)w-2+(w/4)cos(pi/w). Gibbs variational principle gives the lower free-energy rate; Hcrit>=0, W<=L-2 and N<=L-1 give the matching upper bound. For fixed m, a contraction to the labeled cube, an orbit-counting collision bound, a one-dimensional discrete diagonal trace inequality, and the reflecting-exclusion heat-kernel estimate give a uniform O_m(1) sector bound. The independent audit found a missing L^2 factor in the written kinetic consequence; it has been corrected in equations (9)-(11), and the constants then imply (12).
supplied_inputs: Open chain, fixed J,tau, bounded lambda, and a convergent bounded sequence g_L->g<0. No particle-number cutoff or eigenbasis is supplied.
acquired_inputs: Finite-sector comparison and reflecting-exclusion heat-trace bound are proved in the result. The finite-g attractive Lieb-Liniger form is only noted as lower bounded and trace class; lattice-to-attractive-LL convergence is not claimed.
costs: The trial has L-1 qubits and O(L) single-qubit rotations, with O(L) observable evaluations. A conservative total state error delta requires O(log(L/delta)) angle bits per rotation; delta=O(L^-3) controls the variational exponent at O(1) under the stated operator scale. Full partition evaluation still has dimension 2^(L-1). No sampler or sampler lower bound follows. Exact algebra checks pass for three boundary ramps; they are finite evidence only.
baseline: The fixed-m attractive Lieb-Liniger contact operator is lower bounded and has finite heat trace; this does not bound the grand-canonical lattice tail. The coherent ramp supplies a macroscopic-occupation trial with subleading critical-gradient cost.
falsifier: An error in the exact endpoint-inclusive form identity or ramp expectations, failure of the variational upper/lower matching, or a counterexample to the corrected fixed-m trace estimate. A scoped independent audit checked the fixed-m constants after the L^2 correction.
